title: Banking Explorer
intro: A guided, India-specific tour of how a first bank account works, with the official sources behind every fact.
disclaimer: RupeeRise is a learning tool. It cannot open, link or check a real bank account, and it never asks for Aadhaar, PAN, account numbers, PINs, OTPs, card details or document photos. Rules change: confirm current details with your bank or the official source linked on each stop.

stops.title: Can someone my age have a bank account?
stops.story: Hyderabad student Meera is 15 and wants a place to keep her scholarship money. Her friend says she must wait until she is 18.
facts: RBI allows a minor of any age to open and operate a savings account through a parent or legal guardian.
A minor aged 10 or above may be allowed to open and operate a savings account independently, up to limits and terms each bank sets based on its own risk policy.
A minor's account cannot be overdrawn: it must always stay in credit.
Banks still do customer due diligence (KYC), and when the minor turns 18 the bank takes fresh operating instructions.
stops.question: Which statement matches the RBI rule?

options.text: Only adults can have bank accounts, with no exceptions.
options.explanation: Not so. RBI allows minors to have savings accounts.

options.text: A minor can have a savings account through a guardian, and from age 10 may operate one independently within the bank's limits.
options.explanation: Right. The bank sets the exact limits, so always ask the bank what applies to you.

options.text: A minor can overdraw the account if the bank agrees.
options.explanation: RBI says minors' accounts must always remain in credit.

stops.title: What will a bank ask me to show?
stops.story: Meera's guardian takes her to a bank branch. A message that evening says: 'Send a photo of your ID on WhatsApp to finish opening your account.'
facts: Banks must verify who you are (called KYC or customer due diligence) under RBI rules.
Which documents are accepted depends on the bank and the account type, so ask the bank directly.
You share identity documents only with the bank itself, inside the branch or its official app or website that you opened yourself.
RupeeRise never asks for any ID number, document or photo, and it cannot open a real account.
stops.question: A message asks you to send ID photos on WhatsApp to 'finish opening' an account. What is the safe move?

options.text: Send the photos quickly so the account is not cancelled.
options.explanation: Pressure to hurry is a warning sign. Documents are never needed over chat.

options.text: Do not send anything. Check with the branch or the bank's official app or website you opened yourself.
options.explanation: Correct. Real banks handle documents at the branch or in their official app.

options.text: Send only the Aadhaar photo and keep the rest.
options.explanation: Any identity document can be misused. Do not send any of them over chat.

stops.title: Fees and minimum balances
stops.story: Two accounts look the same, but one will charge Meera if her balance dips below a limit.
facts: Some banks offer a basic account with no minimum balance requirement (RBI calls it a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account), with limits on free withdrawals and no cheque book as standard.
Other accounts can have minimum balances, charges or limits on free transactions.
Before opening, ask for the bank's schedule of charges and read what happens if the balance is low.
Terms change, so confirm the current rules with the bank.
stops.question: What is the smartest thing to do before choosing an account?

options.text: Pick the account with the nicest app.
options.explanation: A nice app does not tell you the charges.

options.text: Ask the bank for its list of charges and minimum balance rules, and compare.
options.explanation: Yes. Fees and limits are in the schedule of charges, so ask to see it.

options.text: Assume every savings account has the same charges.
options.explanation: Charges and minimum balances differ between banks and account types.

stops.title: PIN and OTP hygiene
stops.story: Meera gets a UPI 'collect request': 'Enter your PIN to receive ₹2,000.'
facts: Your UPI PIN authorises money going out of your account.
NPCI says to keep your UPI PIN confidential, and that your bank's customer support will never ask for it.
To get paid, you only need to share your UPI ID or QR code.
Never share an OTP with anyone who asks for it.
stops.question: A request says 'Enter your UPI PIN to receive money'. What does that tell you?

options.text: It is how the money gets credited.
options.explanation: Receiving money does not need your PIN.

options.text: It is a scam sign. A PIN is only for sending money, so decline and report it.
options.explanation: Right. Decline the request and report it in your payment app.

options.text: It is safe if the amount is small.
options.explanation: The size does not matter. Entering the PIN approves a payment from you.

stops.title: Is the money in a bank safe?
stops.story: Meera's uncle has ₹3 lakh in one bank and ₹4 lakh in another, and worries about what happens if a bank fails.
facts: Bank deposits in insured banks are covered by DICGC, a subsidiary of RBI.
The cover is up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, including principal and interest.
The limit applies separately to each bank, and the bank pays the premium, not the depositor.
Banks display the DICGC details. The list of insured banks is on the DICGC website.
stops.question: Uncle has ₹3 lakh in Bank A and ₹4 lakh in Bank B (both insured). How much of each is covered by deposit insurance?

options.text: Only ₹5 lakh in total across both banks.
options.explanation: The limit applies to each bank separately.

options.text: All ₹3 lakh in Bank A and all ₹4 lakh in Bank B, since each is under ₹5 lakh per bank.
options.explanation: Correct. The ₹5 lakh limit is per depositor per bank.

options.text: Nothing, because deposit insurance is only for companies.
options.explanation: It covers individual depositors in insured banks.

stops.title: If something goes wrong
stops.story: Meera loses money to a fake collect request. Her cousin also has a different problem: a bank has not answered a complaint about a wrong charge.
facts: For online money fraud, report quickly: call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 and file on cybercrime.gov.in. Speed improves the chance of stopping the transfer.
For a service complaint against a bank, complain to the bank first and keep the reference number.
If the bank does not reply within 30 days, or you are not satisfied, you can go to the RBI Ombudsman at cms.rbi.org.in, within 90 days, free of charge.
Ask a trusted adult to help.
stops.question: Your bank has not replied to a complaint about a wrong charge for over 30 days. What is the official next step?

options.text: Pay someone online who promises to recover the money.
options.explanation: Recovery agents who ask for fees are a common scam.

options.text: Escalate to the RBI Ombudsman through cms.rbi.org.in, keeping your complaint reference.
options.explanation: Right. It is free, and you must have complained to the bank first.

options.text: Post about it publicly and wait.
options.explanation: That does not start any official process.

stops.title: The official way to open an account
stops.story: Meera is ready. Which route is safe?
facts: Visit the bank's branch with your guardian, or start from the bank's own official website or app that you typed or downloaded yourself.
Never use links in SMS, WhatsApp or social media messages to apply or 'verify'.
RupeeRise teaches how this works. It cannot open, link or check any real account, and it will never ask for account numbers, PINs, OTPs or documents.
stops.question: Which is the safest way to start opening a real account?

options.text: Tap a link in an SMS that says 'Zero-balance account in 2 minutes'.
options.explanation: Links in messages are a common way to steal details.

options.text: Go to the branch with a guardian or use the bank's official app or website you reached yourself.
options.explanation: Yes. You control where you end up.

options.text: Ask RupeeRise to open one for you.
options.explanation: RupeeRise is a learning tool and cannot open real accounts.
